issues.label: Definition of abuse under DVPA
issues.why: Court must apply Fam. Code sections 6203/6320 including non-physical abuse and disturbing the peace.

issues.label: Disturbing the peace via social media
issues.why: R.M.'s public posts and username changes directed at A.G. may constitute abuse even without direct contact.

issues.label: Coercive control as abuse
issues.why: Section 6320 includes coercive control, relevant to both parties' allegations.

issues.label: Indirect contact through third parties
issues.why: R.M.'s calls to A.G.'s mother and messages to acquaintances may qualify as abuse.

issues.label: Section 6305 mutual order requirements
issues.why: Court must make detailed findings before issuing orders when both parties request them.

issues.label: Primary aggressor determination
issues.why: Section 6305 requires deciding whether one party was the dominant aggressor.

issues.label: Self-defense analysis
issues.why: A.G. claims her injuries to R.M. were self-defense, bearing on mutual orders.

issues.label: Temporal scope of relevant abuse
issues.why: Court limited evidence to post-December 2023, potentially excluding relevant past abuse.

issues.label: Consideration of past abuse history
issues.why: DVPA permits consideration of entire relationship history, not just recent events.

issues.label: Due process for self-represented litigant
issues.why: Court repeatedly cut off A.G.'s testimony about earlier abuse she sought to present.

issues.label: Right to present evidence at hearing
issues.why: A.G. was prevented from testifying about incidents central to her petition.

issues.label: Standard of proof preponderance
issues.why: DVRO issuance requires preponderance of evidence of past abuse.

issues.label: Reasonable apprehension of future abuse
issues.why: Court must assess likelihood of continued abuse for each petition.

issues.label: Weight of documentary evidence
issues.why: Police photos, neighbor statements, admissions, and messages corroborate A.G.'s allegations.

issues.label: Effect of A.G.'s recantation
issues.why: Recanting the police statement affects credibility but is common in DV cases.

issues.label: Sexual assault allegations as abuse
issues.why: A.G.'s coerced-sex claims constitute abuse if credited.

issues.label: Threats of violence as abuse
issues.why: The gun photo text to A.G.'s friend may constitute threatening conduct.

issues.label: Whether A.G.'s conduct constitutes abuse
issues.why: Court must determine if incessant contact rises to disturbing R.M.'s peace.

issues.label: Relevance of A.G.'s admissions
issues.why: A.G.'s messages admitting harassment support R.M.'s petition.

issues.label: Effect of prior dismissed TRO
issues.why: A.G.'s earlier dismissed TRO may bear on credibility or history.

issues.label: Relevance of PCC no-contact order
issues.why: The mutual college order and both parties' violations inform the analysis.

issues.label: Encouraging suicide as abuse
issues.why: R.M.'s 'pleasekillurself' username may constitute abuse under DVPA.

issues.label: Damage to reputation/privacy as abuse
issues.why: Posting intimate photos and business impersonation may disturb peace.

issues.label: Credibility determinations of both parties
issues.why: Court must weigh conflicting testimony and evidence from each side.

issues.label: Whether R.M. blocked contact voluntarily
issues.why: A.G. argues R.M.'s failure to block undercuts claim his peace was disturbed.

issues.label: Adequacy of findings supporting rulings
issues.why: Court must articulate legally sufficient basis for granting/denying each order.

issues.label: Effect of drug use on the case
issues.why: Both parties' substance use may bear on credibility and conduct.

issues.label: Protection of third parties in order
issues.why: R.M. sought protection for family members, requiring findings as to them.
